current.summary: The staircase runs the full height of the house and changes character as it climbs. Entrance hall: narrow, with the old brown panelled front door (smart lock, fanlight above), terracotta tiles laid diagonally, and a brown door to the ground-floor room. Coats and a cabinet currently fill one side. Lower flights: speckled terrazzo steps and landings; an old painted meter cupboard in the wall. Middle flights: white-grey marble treads. Upper flights: dark stone or slate treads. Landings: one in terrazzo with an arched niche holding an iron fleur-de-lis grille and an urn; one in beautiful old patterned cement tiles (star and lattice design) with a small octagonal window. A wrought-iron scroll balustrade runs all the way up. Walls are cream, with a black-painted skirting band following the stairs, and black lantern-style wall lights at each level. The walls show the recent pipe and cable work: long grey filler patches (pencilled “TUBI” and “2 TUBI 25” where pipes run), white access covers, green tape remnants at ceiling lines, cracks, and peeling paint with old blue-green paint underneath near the top.
keep: Wrought-iron scroll balustrade — the best feature of the stair
Old meter cupboard door (as a period detail)

target.concept: Chosen direction (from the owners' render) — an old Sicilian palazzo / boutique-hotel stair. Upper walls in a tobacco-terracotta limewash with soft, cloudy movement; lower walls in deep olive green to dado height with a moulded top rail; skirting in the same olive; black ironwork; marble, terrazzo and cement-tile floors kept and cleaned. Dressed with framed sepia prints of Sicilian towns under brass picture lights, olive trees in terracotta jars on the landings, a runner in the entrance hall, candles in the niche, and very warm amber lighting.

materials.name: Lower wall: painted dado, or real panelling?
materials.detail: The render shows raised panelling. Three ways to get it: (1) paint only — olive to dado height with a timber dado rail (cheapest, loses no width); (2) rail plus thin applied mouldings forming panels, all painted olive (the render look, about 1–2 cm thick); (3) full timber panelling (most expensive, takes width off a narrow stair). Recommendation: option 2 on landings and the entrance hall, option 1 on the sloping flights.

materials.name: Limewash on the upper walls
materials.detail: Needs a mineral primer over the existing paint, then 2–3 brushed coats. Slightly variable by nature — that is the look.

surfaces.prep: Record pipe runs first. Remove tape. Rake out cracks and fill; scrape peeling paint back to a sound edge; fill and sand the pipe-run patches flush; stabilising primer on chalky areas and on the old blue-green paint; spot-prime filler
surfaces.notes: Stairwell about 12 m high: stair tower / scaffold needed. Work top to bottom
